Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pressR 0.3.0

This is the first release of the successor line developed as 0.2.0.9000; version 0.2.0 itself was never released. It prepares the package for a first CRAN submission:

  • The maintainer address is now raban.heller@uni-ulm.de, the documentation is written in British English (Language: en-GB) and the repository URLs use the canonical CTTIR organisation name. The citation metadata (README, CITATION.cff, .zenodo.json) names the author as R. Heller and uses the title from citation("pressR").

  • The README and vignettes no longer show CRAN status and download badges, which pointed to pages that do not exist before acceptance.

  • Unused suggested packages (‘gganimate’, ‘gifski’, ‘vdiffr’, ‘covr’, ‘pkgdown’) are no longer listed in Suggests.

  • Standardise the named v5 package logo across README, documentation pages and available application headers, with matching light and dark artwork.

  • Reference observations cite their DOI and page: Nyikos et al. (2005), doi:10.21836/PEM20050301, and Armstrong et al. (1998), doi:10.1016/S1067-2516(98)80066-5; the withdrawn legacy entries also carry their DOI. The six-region saddle mask follows the scheme of Nyikos et al. (2005, Fig. 1, p.189) and is no longer attributed to Werner et al. (2002).

  • pr_calc_saddle_slip() decides dominant_side and is_asymmetric from the same comparison: a mean symmetry index exactly at slip_threshold is now "balanced" instead of naming a side while reporting no asymmetry. Its return value is documented field by field.

  • Threshold and duration arguments of the per-frame, summary, regional, gait, hotspot and slip functions must be single finite numbers (durations and slip_threshold non-negative). A character threshold was previously compared as text and silently gave wrong results; NA returned missing values.

  • pr_mask_saddle_6() refuses grids with fewer than three rows or two columns, where its regions used to overlap, and pr_mask_symmetry() refuses an axis with a single grid line. Their handling of odd grid sizes is documented and unchanged.

  • pr_read_mask() rejects non-numeric tokens inside the mask matrix instead of returning missing cells.

  • Recordings without frames no longer produce warnings in pr_calc_seat_hotspot() and pr_calc_regional() (whose regional maxima are now NA instead of -Inf); pr_interpolate() and pr_calc_saddle_slip() explain that there is nothing to interpolate or compare instead of failing with an internal error.

  • Region overlays on pressure maps are drawn as region boundaries instead of one outlined tile per sensor, which hid the pressure picture on platforms and seat mats. pr_plot_foot_report() gives the regional bar chart and the force curve the full width (panel order unchanged), and the composite reports set compact, top-aligned legends side by side on their map and centre-of-pressure panels and drop overlapping map axis labels, so legends no longer overlap panel titles, also at the default figure size of the reference pages. pr_plot_heatmap_masked() refuses unnamed masks, which it used to skip without drawing them; an empty mask list still draws the plain heatmap.

  • The synthetic insole example loads the forefoot in the layout’s metatarsal rows; its peak previously fell into the midfoot region.

  • pr_read_ascii() and pr_read_auto() infer the horse (248 sensors) and bicycle (192 sensors) saddle layouts from a System: saddle_mat header, so the file written by pr_example_files("saddle") reads back, including as an upload in the app.

  • The app no longer prints a stray NULL before a recording is loaded, and its on-screen tables show six significant digits; downloads and reports keep full precision.

  • The saddle report scales its composite figure to the text width; in PDF reports the right-hand panels were previously cut off at the page edge.

  • The tests read a synthetic Novel/Pliance saddle export, tests/testthat/fixtures/synthetic_saddle_MS.asc, written by data-raw/synthetic_saddle.R with invented header values. Its pressures are designed in a test helper, which is the ground truth for the reader, stride, symmetry, regional and sensor-quality tests.

  • The documentation of the cohort, provenance, symmetry, sensor-quality and temporal functions describes them in general terms instead of quoting figures from one data set, and the cohort and provenance tests use synthetic designs. The two design checks that needed a local design file now run on a synthetic cohort instead of being skipped.

This is an explicitly versioned successor. Version 0.1.0 and its manuscript contract remain preserved at commit 5f5b370 and in the baseline audit records.

  • Recognise Novel Pliance content through automatic import and temporary upload filenames; reject malformed numeric fields and contradictory sampling rates.
  • Make generic ASCII and CSV imports strict. Missing sensor values no longer become zero; mismatched widths are no longer padded or truncated. Exported timestamps and sensor IDs round-trip without default-rate substitution. Inferred layouts now align named wide columns and reject incompatible long-form sensor identities. Optional Pliance channel order uses exact field matching.
  • Refuse numeric text outside the supported non-zero magnitude range 1e-290 to 1e290, and conversions with gross disagreement or underflow. These checks prevent observed parser corruption at extreme values and cost additional import time; exact binary replay uses version 2 bundles.
  • Validate stored layout and trial dimensions before analysis. Use scaled arithmetic when finite measurements would otherwise overflow or underflow, and report unrepresentable results explicitly. Missing saddle regions yield an unknown bridge result instead of a negative finding.
  • Add checksum-verified bundles preserving typed metadata and full layout context. Version 2 additionally preserves exact binary measurements and timing; the CSV remains an inspection/exchange view. Version 1 reading retains its decimal precision limitations. Bundle input must come from a trusted source.
  • Preserve existing CSV/report outputs after reported replacement failures, including on Windows; retain and report a backup if restoration fails. Refuse symbolic-link destinations using the portable fs dependency. Archive member aliases no longer silently overwrite an earlier selected member.
  • Correct force-sensor units, unknown calibration, grid-coordinate plots, mask indexing, and all-zero summaries. Coordinate exports use x, y and an explicit unit; rollover uses cop_x, cop_y and coordinate_unit. Interpolation exposes x_grid/y_grid, not fictitious millimetres. COP paths use adjacent valid frames; mean velocity is weighted by observed time. Duplicate COP timestamps are rejected.
  • Preserve declared cohort factor levels and reject conflicting contracts.
  • Separate corrected temporal analysis, historical-method re-execution and measurement-bound reference replay. Corrected sampling and numerical plateau handling intentionally change some historical cycles. Exact replay requires saved cycle boundaries; legacy execution alone cannot promise it.
  • Correct attribution of the six saddle observations to Nyikos (2005), and withdraw unsupported legacy numbers. Reference overlays require source-compatible units, species, gait and mask definitions; reports enable no overlay by default.
  • Add HR/RR workbook import with original cells and source positions, image metadata registration without invented temperatures, bounded archive extraction, source inventories and explicit-key modality linking. Identical files retain identities.
  • Add Shiny comparison uploads, temporal profile selection, real report downloads, selected-mask CSV/report exports, failed-upload state clearing and a configurable 128 MiB upload default. Application launch restores previous options.
  • Render reports in isolated temporary directories and replace completed outputs only after success. Add unit/availability tables and provenance. Treat recording names and metadata as literal report text. Foot report plots and timing tables use separate readable panels; missing provenance is explicit.
  • Add jsonlite, digest and fs imports; readxl, archive and fixture-only writexl are optional dependencies. The successor API snapshot is reviewed independently of the frozen 0.1.0 contract. Declare Shiny 1.6.0, bslib 0.5.0 and testthat 3.2.0 minimums for the application accessibility and test mocking APIs used by this version.

pressR 0.1.0

Initial release

Parsers

  • pr_read_ascii(): Parse ASCII pressure data exports.
  • pr_read_csv(): Parse generic CSV pressure data (wide or long).
  • pr_read_forcesensor(): Parse force sensor data.
  • pr_read_mask(): Parse region mask files.
  • pr_read_auto(): Auto-detect and dispatch.

Sensor Layouts

  • pr_layout(): Construct custom layouts.
  • pr_layout_insole(), pr_layout_platform(), pr_layout_mat(), pr_layout_saddle(), pr_layout_seat(), pr_layout_glove(): predefined layouts.
  • pr_layout_list() lists available layouts.
  • pr_validate_layout() validates a layout.

S3 classes

  • pr_layout, pr_trial, pr_dataset, pr_cop, pr_mask.

Region Masks

  • pr_mask(), pr_mask_default(), pr_mask_apply(), pr_mask_saddle_6(), pr_mask_symmetry(), pr_mask_foot_auto().

Per-frame and trial analysis

  • pr_calc_peak_pressure(), pr_calc_mean_pressure(), pr_calc_force(), pr_calc_contact_area(), pr_calc_cop(), pr_calc_loaded_rate(), pr_calc_pti(), pr_calc_impulse(), pr_calc_contact_time(), pr_calc_cop_path(), pr_calc_cop_excursion().
  • pr_summary(): comprehensive trial summary.
  • pr_calc_symmetry_index(), pr_calc_regional().

Application-specific analysis

  • Gait: pr_calc_gait_cycles(), pr_calc_rollover().
  • Saddle: pr_calc_saddle_bridge(), pr_calc_saddle_slip().
  • Seating: pr_calc_seat_hotspot().

Reference thresholds

  • pr_ref_saddle(), pr_ref_diabetic_foot(), pr_ref_wheelchair().

Visualisation

  • pr_plot_heatmap(), pr_plot_heatmap_masked(), pr_plot_3d(), pr_plot_force_time(), pr_plot_pressure_time(), pr_plot_cop(), pr_plot_cop_butterfly(), pr_plot_contact_area(), pr_plot_regional_bar(), pr_plot_symmetry(), pr_plot_comparison(), pr_plot_saddle_report(), pr_plot_foot_report().

Export and reporting

  • pr_export_csv(), pr_export_report().

Batch processing

  • pr_batch_summary(), pr_merge_trials().

Shiny application

  • pr_run_app(): interactive 6-tab data explorer.

Example data

  • pr_example_trial(), pr_example_files().

Utilities

  • pr_interpolate(), pr_filter_time(), pr_downsample().
